agree.reason: A remote hire who is weighing whether to leave gets an acknowledgement and two reasons, but no stipend, no review date and no sign that the five project leads already come in, so they have little to convince them to stay.

honest.reason: The figures match the brief and it openly says remote work is not the only cause, though 'it is costing us work' and the overhearing-at-desks explanation go a little further than the two client comments and the review data show.

works_the_facts.reason: Beyond splitting the 15 into 4 and 11 and turning 'end of next year' into dates, it derives nothing: no commute cost against the $150 subsidy, no project-lead figure, and no account of what the 30% delay costs over time.

right_comparison.reason: It suggests that staying remote means more lost bids and slower development, but never sets out what continuing as now would look like or show any trend beyond one year's losses.

qualification.reason: The hedge 'we don't think remote work is the only cause' names nothing the reader can check, and the six-month review the user could commit to, with its date and what happens if the policy isn't working, is missing.

objections.reason: It recognises that the remote terms are changing and that partners will come in too, but leaves out the commuting subsidy, the desks arriving in August, the 5 of 6 project leads already in, the review, and a clear statement that there are no exceptions beyond the four.

fit.reason: It is a one-page email in the right form, but it uses placeholder signatures instead of Paul's name and leaves out the meeting time, the location and who to contact (Paul or HR) before Friday.
